title: Tool schema debug route has no route-level authentication or authorization guard
reasoning: The SDK router is created without dependencies, and the GET /api/sdk/tool-schemas handler accepts network-controlled query parameters including user_id, model_id, and model_provider before returning the effective config snapshot plus canonical and provider tool schemas. Within the shown file there is no request, identity, permission, or debug-mode dependency on this route, so any caller able to reach the router can request schema/config projections for arbitrary supplied user/model context. This can expose internal tool availability and provider-specific schema shaping across a network trust boundary. Confidence is medium because application-level middleware outside the provided excerpt could still enforce access control, but there is no route-local protection in the owned file.
recommendation: Add an explicit authorization/debug-access dependency to this route or the /api/sdk debug route group, and bind user_id to the authenticated principal instead of trusting an arbitrary query parameter when access is user-scoped.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the route excerpt shows no test-only guard or assertion of required auth behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test that unauthenticated requests to GET /api/sdk/tool-schemas are rejected, and an authorized request can only retrieve schemas for the permitted user/model context.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/routes/sdk/router.py plus the focused backend route tests for SDK debug access control.
